To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MOMP of each of the seven human serovars examined contains more than one serospecific epitope and that each of the serospecific epitopes is located in one of three discrete subregions within the MOMP.
the major outer membrane protein (MOMP) of Chlamydia can possess more than 1 serovar-specific MOMP epitope.
the major outer membrane protein (MOMP) of a single Chla mydia trachomats serovar can contain more than one serotype-specific B-cell epitope.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying B-cell epitopes in the MOMP of human chlamydias.
the identification of the epitopes in the major outer membrane protein (MOMP) of Chlamydia which are responsible for serovar-specificity.
the development of an outer membrane protein-based chlamydial vaccine.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the major outer membrane protein, the major target of the human immune response to chlamydial genital infection, can possess multiple serovar-specific antigenic determinants, and these serovar-specific determinants are located in three distinct regions of the molecule.
the MOMP of a single serovar of C. trachomatis can possess more than 1 epitope that is serovar specific and that these epitopes are located in 3 discrete subregions of MOMP.
the MOMP of a single serovar can have two or more serovar-specific antigenic sites, which may be located in any one of four VS regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MOMP of C. trachomatis possesses multiple serovar-specific neutralizing epitopes.
the VS regions of a single Ch. trachomatis MOMP can harbor more than one serologically defined epitope and that each serovar-specific MOMP epitope can be neutralizing in vitro.
the major outer membrane protein (MOMP) of Chlamydia serovar F possesses two distinct serovarspecific epitopes, while the MOMP of serovar K possesses three distinct serovars-specific epitopes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same MOMP can harbor multiple epitopes that are specific for different chlamydial serovars, and that these epitopes are clustered in three discrete regions within the VS regions of the MOMP.
a single Chlamydial major outer membrane protein can contain multiple serovar-specific immunodominant B-cell epitopes.
a single MOMP can possess more than 1 serovar-specific MAb-defined epitope and that the epitopes reside in 3 discrete subregions of MOMP, which may be useful for the design of MOMP subunit vaccines.
